question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=-\frac{3}{2}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{3}{2}) & =(-\frac{3}{2})-\frac{(-3/2)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(-3/2)^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(-3/2)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯ \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{2}) & =-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{{3}^{3}}{{2}^{3}\cdot 3!}-\frac{{3}^{5}}{{2}^{5}\cdot 5!}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(-3)^{2n+1}}{{2}^{2n+1}(2n+1)!}+⋯ \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{2}) & =-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{27}{8\cdot 3!}-\frac{243}{32\cdot 5!}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(-3)^{2n+1}}{{2}^{2n+1}(2n+1)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{2}).$
